# zekniri

> zekniri atomically deploys a `configs/` tree into `~/.config`. Three layers stack
> (defaults → `__custom__` → manifest `preserve`), two install modes exist
> (local checkout / remote cache), the engine is pure Python stdlib (3.11+, for
> `tomllib`). Repo = source of truth; `~/.config` = derived state.

This is the LLM-friendly reference: one topic per page, self-contained, load on
demand. Source code is always the final truth; this wiki mirrors it.

## Architecture

- [overview](overview.md): the model, the two axes, the deploy verb
- [file-preservation](file-preservation.md): Dunder `__custom__` vs manifest `preserve` (two mechanisms, on purpose)
- [manifest-schema](manifest-schema.md): `.module.toml` + `.optional-apps.toml`
- [configuration](configuration.md): engine-level `ZEK-niri.conf` (language, wallpapers, log, noctalia picker)
- [install-modes](install-modes.md): repo vs cache vs system, update paths
- [testing](testing.md): TempEnv isolation, test shapes

## Source of truth

- `install.sh`, `zekniri/**/*.py`, `configs/**` — the code. This wiki is a mirror.

## Shipped configs

`configs/` currently holds: `alacritty`, `cava`, `fastfetch`, `kitty`,
`niri` (with `cfg/` and `animations/`), `noctalia`, `waybar`.
Wallpapers live in `assets/wallpapers/` (deployed to `~/图片/wallpaper`, i.e. `<Pictures>/wallpaper`).
Per-app manifests only declare what is exceptional — see
[manifest-schema](manifest-schema.md). `niri` and `waybar` use `preserve`/`chmod`;
the rest use defaults.
